about: Outlaws mutilated her nose during a hunt. Later Daenaera’s companion, she confessed to wishing the queen dead and became a septa.
Robin was Ronnel Penrose and Elaena Targaryen's eldest child and only son. He was presumably the Penrose heir, although this has not been confirmed. His younger sisters were Laena, Jocelyn and Joy.

Laena was the eldest daughter of Ronnel Penrose and Elaena Targaryen, with an older brother, Robin, and two younger sisters. Her mother handled the crown's finances while Ronnel formally held the office of master of coin
Jocelyn was Ronnel Penrose and Elaena Targaryen's second daughter, younger than Robin and Laena and older than Joy.
Joy was the youngest daughter of Ronnel Penrose and Elaena Targaryen, after Robin, Laena and Jocelyn.
Fireball killed her sons at the Mander crossing, sparing the youngest out of pity for her.
Her childless marriage to Aerys was reportedly unconsummated. He refused advice to set her aside; she prayed daily for a child.
He unhorsed Tybolt Lannister at Ashford but lost their ensuing fight despite breaking Tybolt’s sword.
An elderly, ailing lord at the outbreak of the War of the Five Kings.
Lord of Last Hearth in an earlier generation.
The Drunken Giant helped defeat Raymun Redbeard’s wildlings at the Long Lake.
The Lord of Last Hearth known as Hoarfrost.
Hoarfrost Umber's unnamed son was the father of the Greatjon and a brother of Mors Crowfood and Hother Whoresbane.
Crowfood joined Stannis with boys and old men. His scouts helped Theon and Jeyne after their escape from Winterfell.
He brought Umber men to the Boltons while the Freys held the Greatjon hostage.

A knight of Seagard.
He rode at Ashford in 209 AC and was knocked unconscious early in the tourney.
His friendship with Loron Greyjoy was remembered as tragic; the details remain untold.
Lord of Seagard, otherwise unnamed in the surviving references.
The experienced commander of the Shadow Tower withdrew from the election after Sam persuaded him to support Jon Snow.
Jason Mallister's unnamed parent was a sibling of Denys Mallister. This branch connects the Lord of Seagard to his uncle, the long-serving commander of the Shadow Tower.
He killed Rodrik Greyjoy defending Seagard, then fought for Robb. Threats to execute his captive son finally forced him to surrender his castle to the Freys.
He rode with Robb’s companions in the Whispering Wood. Captivity after the Red Wedding made him the Freys’ leverage against Seagard.
Chosen by Visenya to train Maegor on Dragonstone, Gawen had a reputation as one of the realm's most dangerous knights. The young prince took readily to swordplay under his instruction.
The unnamed Lord of Heart's Home and father of Leowyn and Corwyn Corbray. Impressed by his younger son's prowess, he gave Corwyn the family's Valyrian steel sword, Lady Forlorn.

The Apple Counter handled the finances nominally entrusted to Martyn Tyrell under Jaehaerys.
At Ashford he abandoned Dunk for Aerion’s promised lordship. Raymun answered the betrayal by founding the green-apple branch.
A knight of Cider Hall during the War of the Five Kings.
A Golden Company sellsword claiming birth at Cider Hall, where, he said, a knight’s son raped his mother.
Garlan’s wife treated Sansa kindly at court. Her exact Fossoway branch is not identified.
Steffon’s defection made him seek his own knighthood so he could defend Dunk. His green apple distinguished a new branch of House Fossoway.
An amiable knight of the green-apple Fossoways.
Jeyne belongs to the green-apple Fossoways of New Barrel and is married to Ser Gunthor Hightower.
Wyl raiders attacked her wedding, killed Lord Oakheart and sold her into slavery.

Ryam Redwyne unhorsed him at the King’s Landing tourney in 58 AC.
His son’s birth occasioned a tourney at Old Oak in 73 AC.
Prince Baelon unhorsed him at Old Oak’s tourney in 73 AC.
A tourney celebrated his birth at Old Oak.
